Conditioning on the telegraph path, the last-reset age has a continuous density; on each holding interval variation of age pushes through the scalar flow with derivative equal to the nonzero reset-point drift times a positive flow derivative. This gives interior absolute continuity and finite age excludes endpoint atoms. Extend the fluxes by zero outside the accessible interval: the distributional forward equations have only the origin source, hence the endpoint traces vanish. Symmetry and J'=−rp+r delta_0 give J(0+)=r/2. H'=−(r+2lambda)d with g(0)=0 gives density continuity and the stated trace derivative. At the right endpoint J=U−W=r integral_v^v* p>0. Thus the integrating-factor transform of U has positive finite limit because its growth rate is bounded by lambda/Sigma. Taylor expansion at the simple endpoint gives U asymptotic to C(v*−v)^((r+lambda)/k*); integrating the backward W equation gives W/U→lambda/(r+lambda), with W/b one power smaller than U/f. These prove the divergence, critical finite trace, and vanishing cases. The strict coexistence inequalities admit positive rates iff k*>1/2 for k0=1, and continuity plus the origin slope and endpoint divergence forces intervening minima. The zero-current reset-free relation gives the stated curvature and local reversal for 1/2<lambda<1. No higher classification is made at a vanishing cusp slope.
